source.authors: Ao-Ting Hu; Zhi-Gang Lu; Ren-Jie Xie; Min-Hui Xue

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no relevant truncation noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports train–test accuracy gaps and discusses their relationship to membership-inference-based ownership testing, but it does not test any of V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label train and test accuracy and states that ownership verification performance is negatively correlated with generalization ability. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited findings are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates ownership verification using membership inference. Its natural-label accuracies, privacy measurements and verification results do not test V1–V8. Selecting samples by their own-label loss sensitivity does not test whether removing memorized examples lowers held-out accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the basic-method findings but understates the paper's main conclusion: enhanced VeriDIP selects less-private samples to improve ownership verification and reduce sample exposure, including on the tested utility-preserving DP models. The reported negative relationship with generalization concerns verification difficulty across the evaluated configurations, not a controlled causal result.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates privacy-leakage fingerprints for model ownership, not the interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and generalization level; MI attack choice; number and selection of exposed samples; DP privacy budget and hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the evaluated configurations, Adult and Health models have smaller reported train–test gaps than the image models. Basic global-threshold ownership verification generally fails on Adult and Health, whereas per-sample verification succeeds with hundreds to thousands of exposed samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller train–test accuracy gaps can coincide with harder membership-inference-based ownership verification; this comparison does not isolate generalization from dataset, architecture or training differences.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
record.problems: The reported accuracy gaps and ownership results are tied to the evaluated datasets and training configurations. The paper does not establish a causal mechanism between generalization and ownership-verification performance, and reports no uncertainty estimates for the extracted gap values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant results omitted. Detailed p-values for ownership verification and DP evaluations were not extracted because they do not measure train–test generalization gaps or any listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on matched image tasks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its relationship to generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Held-out accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Section 4.3 and Figures 2–3 measure sample-specific loss sensitivity and privacy exposure, not V8's removal-induced test-accuracy loss. Different optimizers and batch sizes across different datasets do not establish V4 or V5 comparisons. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels are not compared.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal and retraining comparison for memorized examples.
